key_insight: Neurofibrillary tangle pathology in Alzheimer’s disease shows strong region-specific and solubility-dependent proteomic changes, with the middle frontal and inferior temporal cortices displaying distinct patterns of protein remodeling and disruption.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help explain why some brain regions are more vulnerable than others in Alzheimer’s disease and could guide biomarker or therapeutic target discovery focused on tau-related pathology.
method: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics of inferior temporal and middle frontal cortex tissue from 27 autopsy cases.
Sequential fractionation by protein solubility (TBS, Na2CO3, urea) followed by nanoLC-MS/MS with data-independent acquisition.
Linear mixed-effects models used to compare protein abundance and solubility across Braak NFT stages and regions.
evidence_signal: The study identified 5,573 protein groups, including 452 differentially expressed proteins, 183 bidirectional expression proteins, and 693 differentially soluble proteins across Braak stages and cortical regions.
watch_item: Because the data come from postmortem tissue and regional sampling, findings are observational and may not directly translate to living-patient diagnostics or treatment effects.
paper_title: Brain region- and solubility-dependent proteomic signatures of neurofibrillary tangle pathology in Alzheimer's disease
